GIT_BLOB_BYTES_V1.purpose: Primary identity for every tracked dependency and tracked exact source whose policy requires byte identity.
GIT_BLOB_BYTES_V1.input: Raw bytes of the blob resolved from the tested Git commit and repository-relative path, not bytes read from the checked-out worktree.

CANONICAL_TEXT_V1.purpose: Explicit semantic-text equivalence check when checkout newline transformations are permitted by policy.
algorithm: Replace CRLF with LF, then replace remaining CR with LF.
Do not apply Unicode normalization, whitespace trimming, final-newline insertion/removal, comment removal, or syntax rewriting.
Encode as UTF-8 and hash the resulting bytes.

BINARY_BYTES_V1.rule: Checked-out bytes must equal the Git blob bytes exactly; no canonicalization is permitted.

tests.objective: Prove that dependency identity is derived from an explicit hash domain and is invariant to permitted checkout newline representation without hiding genuine content changes.
preconditions: Run from a clean tested Git commit with no untracked dependency input.
Generate the closure from imports, fixed artifacts, runtime declarations, Julia manifests, and Lean imports; do not use a hand-maintained inclusion list or exclusions.
The 73 v1 paths are a regression corpus. The amended closure count is generated and may increase only through disclosed transitive dependencies.

positive_controls.action: Resolve every generated tracked dependency at tested_commit:path and compute git_blob_sha256 from raw blob bytes.
positive_controls.pass_condition: Every closure row contains tested commit, path, Git object ID, explicit GIT_BLOB_BYTES_V1 domain, and matching raw blob SHA-256; no primary identity is read from mutable worktree bytes.

positive_controls.action: Materialize LF, CRLF, and mixed-newline fixtures with identical decoded text and process them under CANONICAL_TEXT_V1.
positive_controls.pass_condition: All fixtures produce the same canonical_text_v1_sha256 while retaining distinct filesystem_sha256 values.

positive_controls.action: Generate the amended closure in isolated Windows and Linux clean checkouts of the same commit.
positive_controls.pass_condition: Path set, Git object IDs, git_blob_sha256 values, canonical-text identities where applicable, and the domain-separated closure identity agree. Environment and filesystem hashes may differ only where the policy explicitly allows text newline transformation.

negative_controls.mutation: Change a physics-bearing token such as xi1 to xi1 + 1 while retaining valid UTF-8 and newline form.
negative_controls.required_outcome: git_blob_sha256 and canonical_text_v1_sha256 change; closure comparison rejects the file.

negative_controls.mutation: Add or remove non-newline whitespace.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Canonical identity changes and the file is rejected; canonicalization must not trim whitespace.

negative_controls.mutation: Add or remove the final newline.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Canonical identity changes and the file is rejected.

negative_controls.mutation: Prepend a UTF-8 BOM.
negative_controls.required_outcome: CANONICAL_TEXT_V1 rejects the input rather than silently removing the BOM.

negative_controls.mutation: Apply text normalization to an artifact declared BINARY_BYTES_V1.
Add or substitute a required dependency that is absent from the tested Git commit.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Closure generation or custody fails before trusted execution.

acceptance_gates: Every hash field names its domain; an unlabeled sha256 field cannot establish dependency identity.
The three v5 mismatch paths are rechecked from Git blobs and pass under the amended policy without rewriting the old packet.
All generated closure paths are Git-tracked and no unresolved or manually excluded dependency exists.
LF/CRLF equivalence passes and every genuine-content negative control fails closed on both supported platforms.

tests.objective: Prove a non-circular chain in which Lean derives the identity of the actual executed evidence, the receipt binds that identity, and the outer bundle binds the receipt and certificate.
required_binding: The Lean-facing certificate/envelope commits to certificate-format version, computation ID, candidate hash, physics-profile hash, verification-policy hash, calculation-request hash, source-manifest/receipt-set hash, graph hash, ordered node-trace hash, authoritative root set, canonical exact output-value hashes, Julia evidence hash, mandatory challenge-spec/packet/result-set hashes, status ceiling, and scientific/product/production non-promotion flags.
Lean recomputes the domain-separated certificate/envelope identity from parsed canonical fields. It does not accept an asserted certificate identity as a command-line authority.
An independently serialized verification context supplies the expected contract and evidence identities; Lean compares every committed field and reports only the identity it computed.

The verification receipt records the Lean-computed identity and checker/context/file identities; bundle assembly verifies the receipt-to-certificate edge; the bundle hash then commits to both without requiring a circular bundle-hash field inside the certificate.

positive_controls.action: Build the certificate/envelope from one fresh trusted execution and run the versioned Lean checker on those exact canonical bytes and an independently generated expected context.
positive_controls.pass_condition: Lean recomputes and returns the same domain-separated identity recorded by the receipt, and bundle assembly accepts the exact edge.

positive_controls.action: Repeat certificate creation and checking in a separate process from the same canonical request and sources.
positive_controls.pass_condition: All scientific/contract commitments and the computed certificate identity match; only explicitly environmental evidence may differ.

negative_controls.mutation: Substitute a separately valid certificate having the same mathematical outputs but a different computation, candidate, graph, source, or trace identity while retaining the original expected context.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Lean or bundle binding rejects the substitute.

negative_controls.mutation: Supply 00...00, ff...ff, or another caller-chosen accepted identity.
negative_controls.required_outcome: No caller-selected identity can be accepted or echoed as authority; the checker reports only its internally computed identity.

negative_controls.mutation: Change computation, request, candidate, profile, or policy identity to another valid 64-hex value.
Change graph identity, ordered trace content/digest, or any source receipt/set identity.
Change an authoritative root binding or canonical exact output-value hash.
Change Julia evidence identity or mandatory challenge specification, packet, result-set, applicability, or pass disposition.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Rejected or prevented from reaching VERIFIED_EXACT.

negative_controls.mutation: Raise the status ceiling, assert VERIFIED_EXACT inside the runtime execution certificate, or set any scientific/product/production promotion flag true.
Keep the certificate valid but change the receipt's certificate identity or assemble it with a different bundle member.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Receipt or bundle construction rejects the mismatch.

acceptance_gates: The checker command has no authoritative accepted-certificate-hash argument.
Lean computes the certificate/envelope identity and validates every listed binding against independently supplied context.
Every mutation is made one field at a time with a fresh valid transport/file hash, preventing rejection for the wrong reason.
All positive controls pass and all negative controls reject with a stable reason before any output reaches VERIFIED_EXACT.
required_evidence: mutation matrix with exact rejection codes

tests.objective: Prove that complete node type metadata is inferred or resolved from trusted profile/operation contracts and enforced independently of candidate-declared metadata.
required_binding: Source signatures come from trusted source declarations and typed source resolvers.

Derived signatures are inferred from the operation identifier, ordered parent signatures, parameters, exact value shape/rank, dimension quotient, unit rules, representation/index rules, and domain prerequisites.
Output signatures are identical to the independently inferred parent signature and satisfy the profile's root declaration.
Candidate-declared ValueType metadata is compared with the independently determined signature and never supplies the authority used to validate itself.

positive_controls.action: For all 31 source, 160 derived, and 16 output nodes, derive the trusted expected signature and compare every metadata axis with the candidate and computed exact value.
positive_controls.pass_condition: 207/207 nodes pass with a per-node signature receipt; all 16 root values remain identical to v1.

positive_controls.action: Exercise a profile-declared dimension equivalence under the exact quotient lattice.
positive_controls.pass_condition: A legitimately quotient-equivalent dimension is accepted and canonicalized to the declared equivalence class without permitting an undeclared conversion.

negative_controls.mutation: Replace a node's mathematical kind with another parser-valid kind while preserving its numerical payload.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Reject at that node with the expected/observed signature difference.

negative_controls.mutation: Replace semantic type with another profile-valid semantic type.
Replace the physical dimension with a non-equivalent profile-valid dimension.
negative_controls.required_outcome: Reject at that node before operation acceptance.

negative_controls.mutation: Replace the canonical unit convention or claim an undeclared conversion.
Change exact tensor/vector shape or rank while preserving compatible-looking flattened entries where possible.
Replace, reorder, remove, or add an index space, including COLOR to NATIVE_E substitution.
Replace, remove, or add a representation tag, including the reviewed BMHV substitution.
Change a domain label, status, regulator/profile identity, or prerequisite while preserving the exact value.
Keep each node's declared signature locally plausible but connect parents whose independently inferred signatures violate the operation edge contract.

tests.coverage_rule: Generate a mutation for every one of the 207 nodes on every applicable metadata axis. Use a different profile-valid value when one exists; otherwise use a typed synthetic fixture proving invalid or unknown metadata rejects. The generated applicability census and every result must be retained—sampling is not sufficient.
acceptance_gates: All 207 baseline nodes receive complete trusted signature receipts and all 16 exact root values match v1.
Every generated applicable mutation rejects at the intended node with a stable metadata/edge failure code.
The previously accepted COLOR_TENSOR representation, dimension, index-space, and domain mutations all reject.
A metadata-invalid candidate cannot obtain a runtime certificate or any VERIFIED_EXACT output.
The mutation generator's coverage is derived from the frozen graph and trusted signature schema and cannot be manually narrowed.
required_evidence: trusted source/derived/output signature registry or inference receipts

global_acceptance_rule: All three tests must pass in full. Passing counts cannot average away a failed case. Any repair-induced source meaning, physics operation, parent edge, authoritative root value, claim boundary, or mandatory-challenge applicability change requires a broader new scientific review rather than amendment-only review.
